title: Coding & Technical Problem‑Solving 💻
description: Use prompts to generate, explain, debug, and refactor code like a senior developer.

slides.title: The AI as Pair Programmer 👥
slides.content:
# From Syntax to Architecture

LLMs can write code in dozens of languages. But to get production‑ready code, you need more than `Write a function that ...`. You must specify:

- Language, version, and framework.
- Input/output types and edge cases.
- Performance requirements (e.g., O(n log n)).
- Coding style (e.g., PEP8, use comments).
- Error handling.

Treat the AI like a junior developer who needs a detailed spec.

slides.title: The Code Prompt Blueprint 📐
slides.content:
## Specify Everything Upfront

```
Write a [language] function that [task].
- Input: [type, description]
- Output: [type, description]
- Constraints: [time complexity, no external libraries]
- Style: [include docstring, follow PEP8]
- Handle these edge cases: [empty input, negative numbers, etc.]
```

Example:
> `Write a Python function that returns the Fibonacci sequence up to n. Input: integer n. Output: list. Must be O(n). Include docstring and handle n <= 0.`

quizData.question: Why is 'Write a function to sort a list' a weak prompt?

options.text: It doesn't specify the language, sort criteria, or edge cases, leaving too much ambiguity.

quizData.explanation: Ambiguity in programming leads to code that may not compile or meet your exact needs.

slides.title: Code Generation Example 🔧
slides.codeSnippet: Specific prompt yields clean, well‑commented code with error handling.

slides.title: Beyond Generation: Debugging & Explaining 🐞
slides.content:
## The AI as Code Reviewer

You can paste buggy code and ask:
> `Find the bug in this code and explain how to fix it.`

Or ask for an explanation:
> `Explain this regular expression step by step.`

Or refactor:
> `Rewrite this function to be more readable and follow modern best practices.`

Always provide the code as input data and specify the desired output format (e.g., `Point out the bug, then show the corrected code`).

quizData.question: What is the best prompt to fix a piece of code?

options.text: "Here is the code: [code]. It's supposed to [intended behavior]. Identify the bug and provide the corrected code."

quizData.explanation: Giving the code, intended behavior, and a clear instruction leads to the most useful response.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use the AI for Test Generation

Ask: `Write unit tests for this function using Jest. Cover normal cases, edge cases, and error conditions.` This saves hours and improves code reliability.
